varieties.name: Egyptian Pink
varieties.traits: Softneck; pink cloves; long storage life; pungent, flavourful
varieties.note: Source names it 'well-adapted to South African conditions' without specifying which zone(s); softneck types generally need less winter chill than hardneck, so are the safer default for milder/frost-free areas, but this is this pass's general inference, not a source-stated zone.

evidence.quote: Egyptian Pink Garlic: This variety, known for its beautiful pink cloves and long storage life, is well-adapted to South African conditions.
evidence.doc: Softneck Garlic: The Versatile Choice for South African Farms, Graceland Garlic Seed, May 2024

varieties.name: Rocambole
varieties.traits: Hardneck; rich flavour, marbled purple cloves; 4-10 cloves per bulb; needs a distinct winter (cold requirement) to bulb properly; produces an edible flower stalk (scape)
varieties.note: Zones are this pass's inference: the source ties ALL hardneck types (as a group, not this cultivar specifically) to 'regions that experience a distinct winter season' with February-May as the ideal SA planting window — assigned to the zones with real winter cold per the brief's zone key.

evidence.quote: Hardneck garlic, known for its cold hardiness, is particularly well-suited for South Africa's varied climatic conditions. It flourishes in regions that experience a distinct winter season, as the cooler temperatures promote optimal bulb development... February to May is generally the ideal window for planting hardneck garlic in South Africa.
evidence.doc: Hardneck Garlic: The Robust and Flavorful Choice for South African Growers, Graceland Garlic Seed, May 2024

evidence.quote: Rocambole Garlic: This variety is known for its rich flavour and beautiful, marbled purple cloves. It typically produces 4-10 cloves per bulb.

highveld.text: Hard winter cold here best matches hardneck garlic's stated need for 'a distinct winter season' to bulb properly — plant Feb-May.

evidence.quote: It flourishes in regions that experience a distinct winter season, as the cooler temperatures promote optimal bulb development.

high-mountain.text: Same reasoning as highveld — severe frost fits hardneck's winter-chill requirement well, but not independently confirmed for this zone by name.

midlands-mistbelt.text: Moderate frost is assumed sufficient for hardneck chilling, but this is an inference, not a source-stated recommendation.

lowveld-bushveld.text: No sourced recommendation, but softneck types (Egyptian Pink/White) are the more plausible fit given they don't need the same winter chill hardneck does — general horticultural reasoning, not sourced for this specific zone.

subtropical-coast.text: Same reasoning as lowveld-bushveld: frost-free coast likely favours softneck over hardneck, but this is unsourced inference.
